headline: The game found the Mac’s default audio output during loading
currentWork: Continue through audio setup and movie loading, then inspect the first changing frame.
graphicsStatus: The launch cache holds 1,270 of 18,837 packaged graphics stage and layout combinations. The newly added vertex and pixel pair linked as a Metal render pipeline on the M5 Pro.
screenStatus: The game window opens and stays black during the observed loading sequence. A visible image, the menu and gameplay remain unverified.

milestones.title: The game found the Mac’s default audio output during loading
milestones.detail: On a native launch, the game enumerated local audio outputs and read the default device identifier. The game window remained black.

milestones.title: The game passed text parsing and reached Bink video setup
milestones.detail: Loading continued past the previous text-parsing stop. The game entered Bink routines for file access, memory, worker threads and sound.

milestones.title: The game now runs its loading frame loop on Metal
milestones.detail: Metal runs a full-screen triangle and two rectangles into the game’s 4K display target. One 15-minute launch displayed 3,639 frames.

milestones.title: Metal ran the game’s first draw
milestones.detail: The Mac recorded the game’s draw state and replayed its first draw: three vertices that cover the 3,840 × 2,160 display target, with one block of constants read from game memory. The game then asked to display a second frame, and macOS displayed it. Frames 1 and 2 are both black.

milestones.title: Graphics setup finished and the first draw state arrived
milestones.detail: The game created all the render targets, depth targets, views and pipelines it asks for at startup. About 107 seconds in, it cleared its display target and set a triangle-list topology. The Mac runtime has no draw path yet, so the launch stops there. The window still shows the black frame 1.

milestones.title: The game created 18,967 pipeline variants
milestones.detail: The game loads a packaged pipeline with its programs, then asks the graphics device for copies with different depth, stencil or blend state. The Mac now builds those copies. One launch created 18,967 of them from 11,268 depth and stencil records and 15,212 blend records.

milestones.title: More render targets, and one image read through two formats
milestones.detail: The game placed a second 1,280 × 720 integer image at a 256-byte-aligned address and read the first one as a shared-exponent float texture at the same address. It also sized single-sample depth targets and a 16-bit color target. Each launch showed the same black frame 1 in the window.

milestones.title: The game set up its next render targets
milestones.detail: After frame 1 the game placed four more render targets in its own graphics memory: a 2,560 × 1,440 floating-point color target, a 1,280 × 720 integer image, a 3,840 × 2,160 alpha-only target and a 2,048 × 2,048 RGBA target. It created the views it draws through. The Mac compiler also gained the horizontal integer add instruction the game reached, with a hand-written test.

milestones.title: The first frame is black by the game’s own choice
milestones.detail: The trace shows the game cleared its 3,840 × 2,160 display target to black before it asked to display it. A direct look at the game window confirmed an all-black frame.

milestones.title: macOS displayed the game’s first frame
milestones.detail: The game asked to display frame 1. The Mac drew the game’s 3,840 × 2,160 texture into the game window, and macOS reported its display time on the second scanout. All 64 sampled pixels were black. The Mac startup monitor now shows five of five milestones.

milestones.title: The launch ran past the game’s stall timer
milestones.detail: The game stops itself when its frame loop makes no progress for 30 seconds. Waits for the Mac’s code translator had counted toward that limit. The game’s sleep clock now leaves those waits out. The next launch ran 201 seconds, up from about 40.

milestones.title: The game began preparing a surface for drawing
milestones.detail: After Metal completed the first frame-tagged command list, the game ordered access to a texture and recorded a command to fill a render target with its chosen color. The window is still waiting for a displayed frame.

milestones.title: Submitted the first game command list to Metal
milestones.detail: The game acquired frame token 1 and submitted one command list using that token. Metal completed the submission with two synchronization barriers. The Mac startup monitor now shows four of five milestones reached.

milestones.title: The game received frame token 1
milestones.detail: The native display scheduler issued a token for the game to start its first frame. The game then gave that token to its graphics queue with a request to submit one command list.

milestones.title: Startup recorded a GPU timestamp and requested a frame token
milestones.detail: The game passed its 64-bit GPU timing query and asked the display scheduler for a token to begin a frame. A separate native test checked two real GPU timestamps and copied them back in order.

milestones.title: The game passed the GPU progress-marker call
milestones.detail: The native game recorded its 32-bit marker and reached the next graphics query. A separate test sent the write through Metal and verified the exact value after GPU completion.

milestones.title: Startup bound both shader-visible descriptor heaps
milestones.detail: The game queried the GPU clock, reopened a command list and attached both tables its shaders use to find resources and samplers. The next request was a 32-bit GPU write into shared memory.

milestones.title: The game registered its command memory callback
milestones.detail: Startup reached the point where the game registers its own routine for allocating graphics command memory. The next call asks Metal to start a fresh command list.

milestones.title: Native startup passed the cache-line instruction
milestones.detail: The Mac executed the previously missing CLZERO instruction and reached graphics command allocation. An independent native test checked every byte offset in a 64-byte line across five address forms.

milestones.title: Prepared all 1,969 blocks in the startup function
milestones.detail: The Mac build added the 1,405 remaining identified blocks before opening the game. Startup passed the earlier stop and loaded 205 more translated blocks during the run.

milestones.title: Game passed the one-dimensional texture request
milestones.detail: The same native launch uploaded 22 textures, including cube arrays and a 256-pixel color strip, and continued into new startup code. The next stop occurred in a CPU worker.

milestones.title: Game uploaded its cube textures on Metal
milestones.detail: The title accepted both single cubes and cube arrays after creating its color and depth drawing views. On the Mac GPU, a separate test also verified the six face directions at two resolutions.

milestones.title: Game created its Metal depth and stencil view
milestones.detail: The game created a four-sample depth/stencil view after its color view. A separate native test bound a copied color-view handle to a command list. The next title run reached a six-face texture.

milestones.title: Game accepted its native Metal render-target view
milestones.detail: The title stored the new render-target handle and continued to graphics device method 21, CreateDepthStencilView. A one-pixel hardware test drew and resolved four colors through the same type of Metal attachment.

milestones.title: Game passed both four-sample shader views
milestones.detail: A focused title trace confirmed both GPU resources and both shader views. The next call asks to draw into the four-sample color texture. The existing single-sample path also succeeded in this launch.

milestones.title: Game created the multisample depth target
milestones.detail: Both allocation queries and the placed resource succeeded. Metal independently passed a four-sample depth and stencil readback. The next real request was a float depth shader view.

milestones.title: Game created its four-sample shader view
milestones.detail: The real game passed CreateShaderResourceView and requested a four-sample depth and stencil texture. The native platform regression passed, including the three-resource placement test and the new shader view.

milestones.title: Game created its first four-sample Metal target
milestones.detail: Both placement queries and CreatePlacedResourceX completed in the running game. The following call requested a multisample shader view in Direct3D format 28 (RGBA8).

milestones.title: Game accepted four-sample placement details
milestones.detail: The running title passed both allocation queries and reached resource creation. In a separate M5 Pro test, Metal drew four distinct colors into one pixel and resolved them to the expected value.

milestones.title: The game uploaded its volume textures and the full shader test suite passed
milestones.detail: The package produced three 3D texture uploads in the title. All 5,959 translator tests passed across 447 files. A hardware test also preserved four distinct color samples for the next graphics request.

milestones.title: Native startup passed the integer texture and reached a volume texture
milestones.detail: A Metal shader read all four unsigned channel values correctly. A separate 17 × 9 × 5 volume test checked all 837 texels across three resolutions, including padded rows and depth planes.

milestones.title: The game continued after loading new CPU code in the same window
milestones.detail: The running game resumed at each newly compiled address and reached its next texture format in the same process. The standalone Mac executable now contains those 208 new blocks as well.

milestones.title: Passed 10,000 loaded graphics pipelines and tested CPU compilation in place
milestones.detail: A native test called an untranslated function, loaded two arm64 blocks into the running process and returned the expected value. Running the updated standalone executable produced the same result again.

milestones.title: Native game startup passed 9,900 graphics pipelines
milestones.detail: The title opened its Mac window, streamed its local files and loaded Metal functions for 9,962 packaged pipelines. It then requested an untranslated CPU path, which the native compiler is now building.

milestones.title: Finished the 444-stage shader batch and tested compilation at first use
milestones.detail: In one native launch, a command-list test registered a real package record, overwrote the original shader input, then compiled and bound both Metal functions successfully. The game’s first visible frame is still pending.

milestones.title: Three mesh-shader tests drew the expected image on Metal
milestones.detail: A mesh shader generates geometry in GPU workgroups. The native renderer stored that geometry, read it into triangles, and matched 4,096 pixels in each of three original Leonida tests. Five related pixel shaders also passed a new check for groups that survive a discard.

milestones.title: Started the next 444-stage graphics batch
milestones.detail: The 1,200 selected graphics records share 444 unique stages. The startup window counts each stage after it passes validation and Metal compilation. The public batch estimate uses the measured build rate.

milestones.title: The GPU preserved every surviving pixel in four draws
milestones.detail: The test drew 4,096 pixels each time. It discarded exactly 256 pixels at one threshold and 192 at the other, with both possible output colors. A separate buffer-read test also matched all 4,096 pixels for two different addresses.

milestones.title: One native launch prepared 8,680 graphics pipelines
milestones.detail: The larger shader cache let the game pass its previous high of 4,005 packaged graphics pipelines. The next program controls which pixels survive before normal shading continues.

milestones.title: The Mac completed the 774-stage graphics batch
milestones.detail: All 774 stages passed SPIR-V validation and have native Metal libraries. A mesh shader generates geometry on the GPU. The first one tested used 128 threads per workgroup, with a separate Metal vertex program to read the geometry.

milestones.title: The next shader batch now has a progress bar and time estimate
milestones.detail: The public tracker shows how many stages in the selected batch are ready. The Mac startup window refreshes during each batch. A separate M5 Pro test matched all 4,096 pixels for both the zero-iteration and two-iteration cases.

milestones.title: Preparing shaders before launch passed 3,500 render pipelines
milestones.detail: The first 512 graphics records took 104 seconds to prepare from a partly warm cache. The startup window now shows a progress bar for the selected batch and an estimate based on recent compilation speed.

milestones.title: Startup prepared more than 100 packaged render pipelines
milestones.detail: The Mac passed two pixel-mask tests on real GPU hardware. The nested test kept 4,032 pixels and discarded exactly 64. With that change the same game launch passed its previous stop at 27 render pipelines and prepared at least 118.

milestones.title: Loaded the game’s packaged graphics shaders
milestones.detail: The game accepted 27 packaged graphics pipelines. An independent hardware test linked the first pair against a color and depth target. The GPU progress section now tracks graphics and compute programs separately.

milestones.title: Reached the next graphics pipeline format
milestones.detail: The shader translator now handles the wave count and wave ID supplied at compute startup. Both wave widths passed hardware tests on the M5 Pro. Six more compute programs from the package linked on the Mac.

milestones.title: Metal compiled new programs while the same game launch stayed open
milestones.detail: One native launch linked 36 compute programs from the package library, including 23 built during that launch. The package index contains 2,684 distinct compute programs and thread-group configurations.

milestones.title: The game accepted a compute shader loaded during startup
milestones.detail: The game supplied the program and its thread-group settings separately. The runtime matched both, translated the program, and returned a Metal pipeline configured for groups of 8 × 8 threads. The local shader cache keeps the compiled result for later launches.

milestones.title: The game streamed more than 262 MiB in one launch
milestones.detail: The Mac completed the game’s requests against the local package and recorded the number of bytes delivered. Separate tests verified the exact output of a file read and a compressed memory transfer, along with completion and end-of-file results.

milestones.title: The game opened 17 local streaming queues
milestones.detail: The running title created 17 high-priority file queues and a completion array for each. It then continued reading its local package. A completed transfer through one of these queues is the next storage check.

milestones.title: The game uploaded a texture for its shaders
milestones.detail: The game copied 32,768 pixels into its console tile layout. The Mac runtime converted them into a native Metal texture and returned the shader view requested by the game.

milestones.title: Six game render pipelines linked on Apple Silicon
milestones.detail: Metal linked the game’s vertex and pixel stages. A separate test rendered a full triangle through the same two-pass vertex path and matched the Leonida team’s expected pixels.

milestones.title: First game graphics shaders compiled on the Mac
milestones.detail: The game requested its first vertex and pixel shaders during startup. Both compiled to Metal. The first graphics pipeline still needs to link before the game can draw.

milestones.title: The game configured visibility readback and indirect commands
milestones.detail: Four visibility-query buffers are ready for the CPU to read. The game also registered five indirect command layouts, including indexed draws, compute dispatches and mesh dispatches.

milestones.title: Six builder output tests passed on the Mac GPU
milestones.detail: The Mac ran six of the original Leonida team’s GPU checks against the translated builder programs. Each output matched the expected result. The game also advanced into visibility-query setup.

milestones.title: Every ray-tracing builder shader became a Metal pipeline
milestones.detail: All 52 distinct builder programs compiled and linked in the Metal driver through the game’s own calls. The game returned from the builder to continue startup.

milestones.title: The game configured both 4K display textures
milestones.detail: The native run created shader-readable, writable and render-target views on both display textures and entered the game’s ray-tracing setup library.

milestones.title: The game created its first 4K Metal display texture
milestones.detail: The game accepted the tiled memory calculation and received a real Metal texture. Its next call requests a shader view of that image.

milestones.title: The game wrote readable and writable buffer views
milestones.detail: Cache-line writeback works on Apple Silicon. The game completed twelve observed descriptor writes and advanced to its next graphics allocation.

milestones.title: The game created five descriptor heaps
milestones.detail: The native Mac run used the game’s own allocation callbacks and passed its descriptor-address check. It reached the first update to the table.

milestones.title: The game placed its first large Metal buffer
milestones.detail: A hand-written test copied data across two reordered physical pages on the M5 Pro, issued a barrier and a dependent copy, then verified both results from the CPU. The running game reached descriptor-heap creation.

milestones.title: The game closed 581 graphics command lists
milestones.detail: Methods 131 and 132 order GPU memory operations. Both calls now record a full barrier for the startup requests. The game completed command-list setup and advanced to another device method.

milestones.title: The game opened its first graphics command list
milestones.detail: The running title created a command allocator and a direct graphics command list. A separate native test verified list close, allocator reset, and submission of an empty list to Metal.

milestones.title: The game created Metal queues and fences
milestones.detail: The running title created one direct queue, four compute queues, and five GPU fences. A separate native test submitted a fence signal to Metal and verified completion.

milestones.title: The game showed its own Mac window
milestones.detail: The title requested a 3,840 × 2,160 window, showed it, and called Direct3D device creation. The startup monitor remains visible between retries.

milestones.title: Native launches now have a desktop monitor
milestones.detail: The Mac window shows each startup attempt, package reads, and the last stop reason. Its launch button ran the actual arm64 executable. The game also continued past its first sort.

milestones.title: Startup reached the game’s sort routine
milestones.detail: The arm64 run executed 73,032,177 code blocks and made 66,462 host calls before requesting qsort. These counts include repeated execution of the same code.

milestones.title: A translated Xbox call created a Metal command queue
milestones.detail: A hand-written test created the graphics device and a compute queue on the M5 Pro. It checked the queue description, parent device, and release. The running game has yet to submit a graphics command.

milestones.title: The game passed the string scanner
milestones.detail: The native runtime handled six formatted-input calls. Startup then reached the Windows character-classification routines used during text parsing.

milestones.title: The game read across multiple package files
milestones.detail: One run completed 12 DirectStorage opens and 54 reads before reaching the string scanner. Native tests also verified floating-point conversion and overflow.

milestones.title: The game continued through package parsing
milestones.detail: Three 4,096-byte reads completed. Native tests verified vector permutation, grouped byte sums, and signed multiply-add, including overflow.

milestones.title: The game opened a package archive
milestones.detail: DirectStorage allocated a 32 MiB staging buffer. The game opened the local archive read-only and requested its file timestamps.

milestones.title: Controller registration succeeded in the game
milestones.detail: The game registered for gamepad notifications, continued its startup string parsing, and requested the Xbox DirectStorage factory.

milestones.title: The game created its input interface
milestones.detail: The title continued after the scheduling call, read the Mac’s region, and requested notification when controllers connect or disconnect.

milestones.title: The game passed callback startup
milestones.detail: The native executable contained 546,787 arm64 blocks. The game created a seventeenth worker and reached its process scheduling call.

milestones.title: The offline compiler found 4,096 registered callbacks
milestones.detail: The game reached its callback list after native worker startup. One discovery pass identified 61,859 code blocks for the next translation batch.

milestones.title: The game created 16 native workers
milestones.detail: Offline networking initialized, the floating-point checks passed, and the game issued 15 worker resume calls on the M5 Pro.

milestones.title: The game registered its lifecycle callbacks
milestones.detail: The game created its native task queue and advanced through both lifecycle registrations. Independent Mac tests verified worker callbacks and event delivery.

milestones.title: Offline platform runtime initialized
milestones.detail: The game found and called the native implementation of its platform startup interface.

milestones.title: The startup table completed
milestones.detail: The arm64 executable finished all 1,115 entries in the game’s C runtime initialization table.

milestones.title: The game requested graphics memory
milestones.detail: The game opened the M5 Pro’s Metal device. All seven early memory allocations succeeded.

milestones.title: The game entered its executable
milestones.detail: Seven bundled libraries initialized before the game started on its own Mac thread.

milestones.title: Real shaders rendered offscreen
milestones.detail: Two Metal tests used shaders from the game. Both checked the result across 4,096 pixels.

stages.title: Verify the Xbox package against its manifest
stages.detail: The manifest lists the expected SHA-256 fingerprint of each file. All 108 files in Xbox build 1.0.2.1 matched.

stages.title: Compile and link Xbox shader batches for Metal
stages.detail: The Mac compiled a batch of 2,638 shader entries into Metal libraries. A separate set of 207 pixel shaders linked across 86 graphics pipeline configurations.

stages.title: Verify offscreen rendering with game shaders
stages.detail: Two tests ran game shaders on the M5 Pro. One drew a solid color and the other drew a gradient. Each test checked all 4,096 pixels against its expected result.

stages.title: Translate x86-64 startup code to arm64
stages.detail: The first startup build linked 88,740 blocks of Xbox CPU instructions into a Mach-O executable, the format macOS runs directly. The build that passed callback startup contained 546,787 arm64 blocks.

stages.title: Load the executable and initialize its libraries
stages.detail: The Mac loader mapped the Xbox executable and seven bundled libraries. All seven initialized, and two callbacks for thread-local storage returned before the game reached its entry point.

stages.title: Initialize memory and the offline Xbox runtime
stages.detail: The game opened the Metal device and made seven successful virtual-memory allocations. Its 1,115-entry C initialization table finished, and the offline Xbox runtime started.

stages.title: Connect the Xbox task queue and app-state callbacks
stages.detail: The game created its Xbox task queue and registered both lifecycle handlers. A translated-code test ran a callback on a separate Mac thread. Local event tests delivered suspend, resume, and focus changes.

stages.title: Complete offline platform startup
stages.detail: The game completed offline startup far enough to register, create, and show its own 3,840 × 2,160 window. It then requested ID3D12Device11, its graphics device interface.

stages.title: Bind Direct3D 12 buffers and textures to Metal
stages.detail: The game bound shared buffers, both 4K display textures and its first uploaded texture to Metal. It linked six render pipelines and read local package data through 17 streaming queues.

stages.title: Submit the game’s GPU commands to Metal
stages.detail: The Mac issued frame token 1. The game submitted its own command list for that frame, and Metal reported completion with two synchronization barriers.

stages.title: Present a game-rendered frame in a Mac window
stages.detail: Metal runs a full-screen triangle and two rectangles into the game’s 4K display target. One 15-minute launch displayed 3,639 frames.
stages.blocker: The game has reached console audio memory setup. Movie decoding and visible imagery remain unverified.
stages.nextTest: Continue through audio setup and movie loading, then inspect the first changing frame.

stages.title: Route keyboard or controller input to the menu
stages.detail: Deliver macOS input events through the interface the game reads. Open the menu, select an option, and verify that the game changes the selection on screen.

stages.title: Stream world assets through a playable scene
stages.detail: Load geometry and textures from the local package. Move the character through the scene and verify that new assets load while input and successive frames continue.
